historical_claims.anchor: In the mid-1980s, Peter acquired a black costume during the *Secret Wars* crossover.
The rejected entity later bonds with Eddie Brock, becoming the villain Venom.
Venom made his full debut in *The Amazing Spider-Man* number three hundred, published in 1988.
*Ultimate Spider-Man* began in 2000, written by Brian Michael Bendis and drawn by Mark Bagley.
Miles Morales first appeared in *Ultimate Fallout* number four in 2011, after the death of the Ultimate universe's Peter Parker.
His subsequent solo series, *Ultimate Comics Spider-Man*, was written by Brian Michael Bendis with art by Sara Pichelli.
It allowed Peter and Miles to coexist as Spider-Man characters in a shared setting rather than requiring one to erase the other.

Her first appearance was in *Edge of Spider-Verse* number two in 2014, created by writer Jason Latour and artist Robbi Rodriguez, with Rico Renzi's coloring a major part of the comic's visual identity.
The major 2014 *Spider-Verse* event, including *The Amazing Spider-Man* number nine, brought different Spider-people together against a multiversal threat.
The film won the Academy Award for animated feature at the 2019 ceremony.
The 2023 sequel, *Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse*, pushes the problem of inheritance in another direction.
Readers of *The Amazing Spider-Man* number two hundred fifty-two saw Peter return in the black suit before the crossover had published the issue showing him acquire it.
Randy Schueller, a Marvel reader, had submitted an idea for a black suit in the early 1980s.
